- Net debt (INR Mn) has risen materially: 4,883 at 31-Mar-2025, 10,538 at 31-Mar-2026 and 11,026 at 30-Jun-2026.

bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Market leadership in India: 19 of its top 20 brands rank among the top three in their respective therapy areas, and the Company ranks #2 in gynaecology and #13 by market share in India
- Complex-product mix: approximately half of India revenue comes from complex and differentiated products (biotherapeutics, injectables, iron formulations, chiral molecules, photochemistry-based therapies) and around 30% of international revenue from complex products
- Brand depth: 32 large brands above INR 500 Mn, up 4x since 2020, with several established brands individually generating over INR 1,000 Mn in annual revenue
- Trusted commercial partner for global innovators: exclusive in-licensing arrangements with Novo Nordisk, Sanofi and Roche reflect confidence in Emcure's Indian distribution and field-force capability
- R&D and first-mover capability across complex chemistry, biologics, NDDS, long-acting injectables and antibody-drug conjugates; first generic entrant in Europe for liposomal Amphotericin B and one of six global voluntary licensees for Gilead's Lenacapavir
- Global reach: presence in over 80 countries with 900+ products launched globally
- Established international front-ends: top-10 generic player in Canada and the largest India-headquartered pharma company by prescriptions there; Tillomed platform in Europe strengthened by 120+ Manx marketing authorisations
- Field-force productivity improvement in India from INR 0.54 million to INR 0.70 million per medical representative per month over two years
- Scale and compliance advantage: stricter Schedule M requirements favour large organised players with existing global GMP-compliant facilities
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export and geographic concentration — Exports contributed 50.26% of the Company's total turnover in FY 2025-26 and international operations accounted for ~56% of consolidated revenue (Europe 20%, Canada 16%, RoW 20%), so currency moves, tariff and trade-policy shifts, and regulatory action in any one region transmit directly to consolidated results. Management identifies international growth as the faster-growing engine, which increases rather than reduces this dependence.
- Acquisition-led leverage and integration risk — Net debt increased to INR 10,538 Mn during FY 2025-26 due to acquisition-related payouts, including the buyout of the remaining 20.4% minority stake in Zuventus and the Manx portfolio acquisition, with further earn-out payments of around INR 3,358 Mn on the Mantra acquisition due in H1 FY 2026-27. Deleveraging over the next 24 months is explicitly conditioned on there being no further large acquisitions. Integration risk is already visible: domestic Q4 growth slowed to 5.2% as the Zuventus consolidation required comprehensive leadership changes and portfolio and field-force restructuring.
- Regulatory, quality and compliance exposure across multiple regulated markets — Management states quality is 'non-negotiable' and that as the Company enters more complex therapies and regulated markets, maintaining consistent standards across sites and products becomes even more important — a loss of that consistency at any single site would threaten market access. Stricter Schedule M compliance raises fixed costs, documentation, validation and data-integrity requirements across the industry. Several pipeline milestones (bevacizumab launch, Lenacapavir registration, Amphotericin B expansion) are explicitly conditioned on regulatory approval.
- Supply chain, freight and raw material cost volatility from geopolitical conflict — Management flags that macroeconomic and geopolitical headwinds, including developments in West Asia and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, have led to higher freight, insurance and certain raw material costs. Mitigation rests on an inventory buffer of one to two quarters across key international markets, which limits but does not eliminate exposure and itself ties up working capital.
- Dependence on a concentrated set of large brands and on in-licensed products owned by third parties — The domestic franchise leans on a small number of large brands — 32 brand families above INR 500 Mn and 10 above INR 1,000 Mn — while several near-term growth drivers (Poviztra from Novo Nordisk, Amaryl and Cetapin from Sanofi, and select nephrology and transplant products from Roche) are in-licensed rather than owned, so the underlying rights, pricing and manufacturing sit with the innovator partner.
- Generic price erosion and intensifying competition from patent expiries — The semaglutide patent expired in India in March 2026, prompting several companies to launch generic equivalents in a market where Emcure has just built its position through the Novo Nordisk partnership; the AR notes a Poviztra price revision in April 2026. Around 635 drugs face patent expiration between 2026 and 2027, which increases competition as well as opportunity, and the Company's own AR notes patent expiries increase competition within the pharmaceutical market.
- High permanent-employee attrition and talent dependence — The BRSR reports a turnover rate for permanent employees of 33% in FY 2025-26 (34% for female employees), broadly in line with 36% in FY 2024-25 and 33% in FY 2023-24 — a structurally elevated rate for a business whose India growth is explicitly attributed to field-force productivity and leadership strengthening, and which has just undertaken large-scale field-force restructuring.
- Single-activity concentration in pharmaceutical manufacturing — The BRSR records that 100% of turnover comes from a single main activity, the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, medicinal chemical and botanical products, across 9 domestic plants with no international plants disclosed. There is no diversifying business line to absorb a sector-wide pricing, regulatory or supply shock, and manufacturing is geographically concentrated in India.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Emcure's FY 2025-26 expansion was primarily portfolio- and geography-led rather than greenfield. Domestically, the Company completed the buyout of the remaining 20.4% minority stake in Zuventus Healthcare, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary with effect from 03 October 2025, and expects backend and operational synergies over time; it also incorporated two new wholly-owned subsidiaries, Emcure Lifesciences Private Limited (17 June 2025) and Emcure Wellness Private Limited (03 July 2025), to support the newly entered dermatology and consumer health and wellness businesses. Internationally, European subsidiary Tillomed Laboratories acquired select assets of Manx Pharma including marketing authorisations, intellectual property rights, product dossiers and inventory, adding 120+ marketing authorisations of which nearly half are yet to be commercialised; the Cutimed acquisition strengthened the dermatology range in Canada. On the product side, Emcure scaled up and secured approvals for liposomal Amphotericin B, becoming the first generic entrant in Europe for this molecule, with registrations and launches expanding across Europe and Rest of World markets in FY 2026-27. The Company operates 9 plants in India (with no international plants disclosed) alongside 1 registered and corporate office, 4 regional offices, 22 C&F locations and 3 warehouses. Physical capex is directed at maintenance, operational enhancements and targeted capacity expansion, particularly to support the scale-up of complex injectables and biosimilars, and management expects FY 2026-27 investment to remain at levels similar to FY 2025-26. On energy infrastructure, a captive solar power capacity of 11.7 MW is under installation at a few plants in Gujarat, of which 5.7 MW is presently operational and the balance will soon be commissioned; on full commissioning the project is expected to generate approximately 91.25 lakh kWh of renewable electricity annually. A cooling-tower energy-efficiency upgradation programme was also undertaken during the year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Emcure is expected to sustain a steady medium-term growth trajectory supported by both domestic and international businesses, with international growth outpacing domestic growth and driving overall expansion
- The domestic formulations segment is expected to grow faster than the overall industry, driven by cardio-metabolic, women's health, oncology, CNS and nephrology therapies
- Domestic growth will also benefit from recovery, improved productivity and the expansion of in-licensed brands, plus new platforms such as semaglutide Poviztra, the dermatology entry and consumer health offerings
- International business is expected to grow faster in the medium term with expansion across Europe, Canada and RoW, driven by complex injectables including Amphotericin B in Europe, market share gains in existing products and new launches
- The RoW portfolio is expected to see higher growth in the non-ARV business, supported by new approvals and product launches
- The Company is increasing its focus on complex injectables, biosimilars and NDDS, and is increasing R&D spending to support this shift
- Productivity gains are being targeted through digital adoption and AI
- Margin lever: continued EBITDA margin expansion expected over the current five-year strategic plan, driven by operating leverage, mix improvement, productivity enhancement and disciplined execution
- Poviztra (semaglutide) uptake has been encouraging, particularly after the price revision in April 2026, and this therapy is expected to build steadily in FY 2026-27
- The Zuventus buyout is expected to generate backend and operational synergies supporting stronger performance over time; the softer Q4 domestic growth was a temporary transition phase from leadership, portfolio and field-force restructuring
- Industry structure tailwind: the Indian pharmaceutical market is expected to maintain healthy growth over FY 2026-FY 2029 with chronic therapies outpacing overall industry growth; the gynaecology segment (Emcure's #2 position) is projected to grow at 8.5%-9.5% CAGR
- The Indian GLP-1 market is expected to grow from INR 10-12 Bn in 2025 to INR 45-50 Bn by 2030, supported by rising diabetes and obesity prevalence, improving affordability and increasing patient awareness
- Patent cliffs are a structural opportunity: around 635 drugs are expected to face patent expirations between 2026 and 2027, and 15 blockbuster drugs worth around USD 112.0 Bn go off patent between 2023 and 2029
- Stricter Schedule M compliance raises barriers to entry and strengthens the competitive advantage of large, organised pharma companies with existing global GMP-compliant facilities
- Input-cost watch: higher freight, insurance and certain raw material costs from Middle East geopolitical developments are mitigated by an inventory buffer of one to two quarters across key international markets, and FY 2026-27 margin guidance already factors in the current pricing environment
- A healthy ARV order book supported international revenue growth in FY 2025-26
- The RoW business combines a strong ARV order book and a next-generation HIV pipeline with expanding non-ARV revenues from complex injectables and biosimilar launches, targeting a USD 2 Bn+ addressable market
- Canada pipeline of 50+ products, including first-generic launches planned for eight near-term molecules covering Amantadine capsules, Treosulfan and Treprostinil injections, Amphotericin B formulations and semaglutide injectables
- Europe: the Manx Pharma portfolio acquisition added 120+ marketing authorisations through Tillomed Laboratories, nearly half of which are yet to be commercialised
- Medium- to long-term R&D pipeline comprising complex chemistry, biologics, NDDS, complex injectables including long-acting injectables, and antibody-drug conjugates
- 25+ new launches in the domestic market and 35+ new launches in international markets during FY 2025-26
- Over the next two financial years Emcure plans several key product launches while deepening its presence in consumer healthcare and dermatology

risks.note: Exports contributed 50.26% of the Company's total turnover in FY 2025-26 and international operations accounted for ~56% of consolidated revenue (Europe 20%, Canada 16%, RoW 20%), so currency moves, tariff and trade-policy shifts, and regulatory action in any one region transmit directly to consolidated results. Management identifies international growth as the faster-growing engine, which increases rather than reduces this dependence.

Net debt increased to INR 10,538 Mn during FY 2025-26 due to acquisition-related payouts, including the buyout of the remaining 20.4% minority stake in Zuventus and the Manx portfolio acquisition, with further earn-out payments of around INR 3,358 Mn on the Mantra acquisition due in H1 FY 2026-27. Deleveraging over the next 24 months is explicitly conditioned on there being no further large acquisitions. Integration risk is already visible: domestic Q4 growth slowed to 5.2% as the Zuventus consolidation required comprehensive leadership changes and portfolio and field-force restructuring.

risks.risk: Regulatory, quality and compliance exposure across multiple regulated markets
risks.note: Management states quality is 'non-negotiable' and that as the Company enters more complex therapies and regulated markets, maintaining consistent standards across sites and products becomes even more important — a loss of that consistency at any single site would threaten market access. Stricter Schedule M compliance raises fixed costs, documentation, validation and data-integrity requirements across the industry. Several pipeline milestones (bevacizumab launch, Lenacapavir registration, Amphotericin B expansion) are explicitly conditioned on regulatory approval.

risks.risk: Supply chain, freight and raw material cost volatility from geopolitical conflict
risks.note: Management flags that macroeconomic and geopolitical headwinds, including developments in West Asia and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, have led to higher freight, insurance and certain raw material costs. Mitigation rests on an inventory buffer of one to two quarters across key international markets, which limits but does not eliminate exposure and itself ties up working capital.

risks.risk: Dependence on a concentrated set of large brands and on in-licensed products owned by third parties
risks.note: The domestic franchise leans on a small number of large brands — 32 brand families above INR 500 Mn and 10 above INR 1,000 Mn — while several near-term growth drivers (Poviztra from Novo Nordisk, Amaryl and Cetapin from Sanofi, and select nephrology and transplant products from Roche) are in-licensed rather than owned, so the underlying rights, pricing and manufacturing sit with the innovator partner.

risks.risk: Generic price erosion and intensifying competition from patent expiries
risks.note: The semaglutide patent expired in India in March 2026, prompting several companies to launch generic equivalents in a market where Emcure has just built its position through the Novo Nordisk partnership; the AR notes a Poviztra price revision in April 2026. Around 635 drugs face patent expiration between 2026 and 2027, which increases competition as well as opportunity, and the Company's own AR notes patent expiries increase competition within the pharmaceutical market.

risks.risk: High permanent-employee attrition and talent dependence
risks.note: The BRSR reports a turnover rate for permanent employees of 33% in FY 2025-26 (34% for female employees), broadly in line with 36% in FY 2024-25 and 33% in FY 2023-24 — a structurally elevated rate for a business whose India growth is explicitly attributed to field-force productivity and leadership strengthening, and which has just undertaken large-scale field-force restructuring.

The BRSR records that 100% of turnover comes from a single main activity, the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, medicinal chemical and botanical products, across 9 domestic plants with no international plants disclosed. There is no diversifying business line to absorb a sector-wide pricing, regulatory or supply shock, and manufacturing is geographically concentrated in India.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Emcure is expected to sustain a steady medium-term growth trajectory supported by both domestic and international businesses, with international growth outpacing domestic growth and driving overall expansion
- The domestic formulations segment is expected to grow faster than the overall industry, driven by cardio-metabolic, women's health, oncology, CNS and nephrology therapies
- Domestic growth will also benefit from recovery, improved productivity and the expansion of in-licensed brands, plus new platforms such as semaglutide Poviztra, the dermatology entry and consumer health offerings
- International business is expected to grow faster in the medium term with expansion across Europe, Canada and RoW, driven by complex injectables including Amphotericin B in Europe, market share gains in existing products and new launches
- The RoW portfolio is expected to see higher growth in the non-ARV business, supported by new approvals and product launches
- The Company is increasing its focus on complex injectables, biosimilars and NDDS, and is increasing R&D spending to support this shift
- Productivity gains are being targeted through digital adoption and AI
- Margin lever: continued EBITDA margin expansion expected over the current five-year strategic plan, driven by operating leverage, mix improvement, productivity enhancement and disciplined execution
- Poviztra (semaglutide) uptake has been encouraging, particularly after the price revision in April 2026, and this therapy is expected to build steadily in FY 2026-27
- The Zuventus buyout is expected to generate backend and operational synergies supporting stronger performance over time; the softer Q4 domestic growth was a temporary transition phase from leadership, portfolio and field-force restructuring
- Industry structure tailwind: the Indian pharmaceutical market is expected to maintain healthy growth over FY 2026-FY 2029 with chronic therapies outpacing overall industry growth; the gynaecology segment (Emcure's #2 position) is projected to grow at 8.5%-9.5% CAGR
- The Indian GLP-1 market is expected to grow from INR 10-12 Bn in 2025 to INR 45-50 Bn by 2030, supported by rising diabetes and obesity prevalence, improving affordability and increasing patient awareness
- Patent cliffs are a structural opportunity: around 635 drugs are expected to face patent expirations between 2026 and 2027, and 15 blockbuster drugs worth around USD 112.0 Bn go off patent between 2023 and 2029
- Stricter Schedule M compliance raises barriers to entry and strengthens the competitive advantage of large, organised pharma companies with existing global GMP-compliant facilities
- Input-cost watch: higher freight, insurance and certain raw material costs from Middle East geopolitical developments are mitigated by an inventory buffer of one to two quarters across key international markets, and FY 2026-27 margin guidance already factors in the current pricing environment
- A healthy ARV order book supported international revenue growth in FY 2025-26
- The RoW business combines a strong ARV order book and a next-generation HIV pipeline with expanding non-ARV revenues from complex injectables and biosimilar launches, targeting a USD 2 Bn+ addressable market
- Canada pipeline of 50+ products, including first-generic launches planned for eight near-term molecules covering Amantadine capsules, Treosulfan and Treprostinil injections, Amphotericin B formulations and semaglutide injectables
- Europe: the Manx Pharma portfolio acquisition added 120+ marketing authorisations through Tillomed Laboratories, nearly half of which are yet to be commercialised
- Medium- to long-term R&D pipeline comprising complex chemistry, biologics, NDDS, complex injectables including long-acting injectables, and antibody-drug conjugates
- 25+ new launches in the domestic market and 35+ new launches in international markets during FY 2025-26
- Over the next two financial years Emcure plans several key product launches while deepening its presence in consumer healthcare and dermatology

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Emcure's FY 2025-26 expansion was primarily portfolio- and geography-led rather than greenfield. Domestically, the Company completed the buyout of the remaining 20.4% minority stake in Zuventus Healthcare, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary with effect from 03 October 2025, and expects backend and operational synergies over time; it also incorporated two new wholly-owned subsidiaries, Emcure Lifesciences Private Limited (17 June 2025) and Emcure Wellness Private Limited (03 July 2025), to support the newly entered dermatology and consumer health and wellness businesses. Internationally, European subsidiary Tillomed Laboratories acquired select assets of Manx Pharma including marketing authorisations, intellectual property rights, product dossiers and inventory, adding 120+ marketing authorisations of which nearly half are yet to be commercialised; the Cutimed acquisition strengthened the dermatology range in Canada. On the product side, Emcure scaled up and secured approvals for liposomal Amphotericin B, becoming the first generic entrant in Europe for this molecule, with registrations and launches expanding across Europe and Rest of World markets in FY 2026-27. The Company operates 9 plants in India (with no international plants disclosed) alongside 1 registered and corporate office, 4 regional offices, 22 C&F locations and 3 warehouses. Physical capex is directed at maintenance, operational enhancements and targeted capacity expansion, particularly to support the scale-up of complex injectables and biosimilars, and management expects FY 2026-27 investment to remain at levels similar to FY 2025-26. On energy infrastructure, a captive solar power capacity of 11.7 MW is under installation at a few plants in Gujarat, of which 5.7 MW is presently operational and the balance will soon be commissioned; on full commissioning the project is expected to generate approximately 91.25 lakh kWh of renewable electricity annually. A cooling-tower energy-efficiency upgradation programme was also undertaken during the year.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leadership in India: 19 of its top 20 brands rank among the top three in their respective therapy areas, and the Company ranks #2 in gynaecology and #13 by market share in India
- Complex-product mix: approximately half of India revenue comes from complex and differentiated products (biotherapeutics, injectables, iron formulations, chiral molecules, photochemistry-based therapies) and around 30% of international revenue from complex products
- Brand depth: 32 large brands above INR 500 Mn, up 4x since 2020, with several established brands individually generating over INR 1,000 Mn in annual revenue
- Trusted commercial partner for global innovators: exclusive in-licensing arrangements with Novo Nordisk, Sanofi and Roche reflect confidence in Emcure's Indian distribution and field-force capability
- R&D and first-mover capability across complex chemistry, biologics, NDDS, long-acting injectables and antibody-drug conjugates; first generic entrant in Europe for liposomal Amphotericin B and one of six global voluntary licensees for Gilead's Lenacapavir
- Global reach: presence in over 80 countries with 900+ products launched globally
- Established international front-ends: top-10 generic player in Canada and the largest India-headquartered pharma company by prescriptions there; Tillomed platform in Europe strengthened by 120+ Manx marketing authorisations
- Field-force productivity improvement in India from INR 0.54 million to INR 0.70 million per medical representative per month over two years
- Scale and compliance advantage: stricter Schedule M requirements favour large organised players with existing global GMP-compliant facilities

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.
